system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
The Seller’s “FINAL” and market-context labels are negotiating positions, not evidence that the terms were agreed. Against the AUD 24m, debt-free/cash-free baseline, I would treat the following as buyer-side positions for the mark-up.

| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General warranty claims capped in aggregate at **20% of price (AUD 4.8m)**. | A materially higher cap, with separate, higher caps for specific risk areas where justified; no cap for fraud or deliberate concealment. | **Counter at 50% of price, with targeted higher caps and appropriate carve-outs** — 20% may leave the Buyer materially underprotected if multiple business warranties prove inaccurate. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 tipping basket, with recovery only above the basket. | A lower de minimis and basket, with a **first-dollar/deductible basket** rather than a tipping basket; define aggregation and related claims. | **Propose AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 120,000 deductible basket** — the Seller’s thresholds and tipping feature can exclude substantial cumulative losses. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | 18 months after Completion; Seller says limitations should apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise. | A longer period for general warranties (e.g. 24 months); distinct periods for tax, fundamental and other claims; no blanket extension of the general period to all claims. | **Seek 24 months for general warranties and bespoke survival periods for other categories** — 18 months may be too short to discover and quantify latent issues. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to the general cap and time limits. | Separate, substantially higher or uncapped protection for capacity, ownership, valid issue and transfer of shares; longer survival, subject to enforceability. | **Reject the general regime for fundamental/title warranties** — defects in ownership or ability to transfer the shares threaten the transaction itself. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims; no express fraud carve-out is stated. | Expressly preserve claims for fraud and deliberate concealment, including appropriate treatment of caps, time bars, exclusive remedy and non-reliance, to the extent permitted by law. | **Add an express fraud carve-out from contractual limitations** — the Seller should not obtain contractual protection for its own fraud. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | Broad disclosure of the entire indexed data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public corporate records, plus specific disclosures. | Specific, fair disclosure against each warranty, with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter; no blanket data-room or public-register disclosure. | **Delete general disclosure and require warranty-specific disclosure** — blanket incorporation can qualify warranties through material the Buyer may not have identified or understood. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known by Buyer or advisers, including matters discoverable from the data room or public records. | No imputed or constructive knowledge bar; at most, a narrowly defined bar for actual knowledge of specified individuals after express disclosure, with agreed treatment of fraud. | **Reject the proposed qualifier** — “discoverable” knowledge turns diligence access into a broad and uncertain waiver of warranty claims. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent. DD-002 shows about AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30%) and conditions under clause 11.3; no final consent or evidence conditions are satisfied. | A condition precedent requiring final, unconditional written consent and satisfaction or waiver of applicable conditions before Completion; termination/long-stop protection if not obtained. | **Make effective consent and condition compliance a Completion condition** — Bluefen’s concentration makes an ineffective or conditional consent a material continuity risk. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | About AUD 3.2m outstanding; release to follow Completion. DD-003 says it remains unpaid and no final security discharge is in the room. | Repayment at or before Completion from the funds flow, lender payout letter, executed releases and evidence of discharge; debt-free/cash-free adjustment and no post-Completion reliance on Seller’s promise. | **Require payoff and release as a Completion deliverable** — a post-Completion release leaves the Buyer exposed to inherited debt and security. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 conditional Completion bonuses omitted from the draft funds flow; payroll tax, super and on-costs not addressed. | Full itemisation and treatment in the completion mechanics (including any employer on-costs); Seller-funded or treated as debt/leakage, without double counting. | **Reconcile and fund the bonuses and on-costs at Completion** — an omitted transaction-triggered liability conflicts with the debt-free/cash-free economics. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment and considered adequate. DD-004 makes transfer conditional on all SOW3 fees being paid; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open but is not independent proof of non-payment, and no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the room. | A specific indemnity covering title, access, use and transfer of all relevant IP/materials and associated loss; require cleared payment evidence and an effective assignment/confirmation by Completion. | **Broaden the indemnity and require transfer evidence as a Completion deliverable** — the disclosed payment condition and missing confirmation leave chain-of-title risk unresolved. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material; no specific protection proposed. DD-006 records a link sent to an unintended external address and a possible ~1,240 records, with access, scope and notification status unknown. | Specific disclosure, continued investigation and cooperation, preservation of records, required notifications/remediation, and a tailored indemnity or escrow/retention for defined incident-related losses. | **Seek a specific incident protection and pre-Completion information/cooperation obligations** — uncertainty about access and notification does not eliminate potentially material privacy exposure. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate) treated as ordinary-course costs. DD-008 and DD-011 should be read together; avoidability, termination, accrual and ordinary-course status are not established. | Confirm terms, timing, termination rights, accrual/payment status and business need; capture any pre-Completion commitment or unpaid amount in the completion accounts/indebtedness or specific covenant. | **Do not accept the ordinary-course characterisation without verification** — the aggregate commitment and its accounting/timing treatment remain unclear. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims; Seller proposes the same limits broadly unless expressly stated otherwise. | Clearly separate general warranty, fundamental/title, tax, specific indemnity, covenant, fraud and other claim regimes, with expressly allocated caps, baskets and survival periods. | **Add an express claims-regime matrix and precedence clause** — blanket limitations risk unintentionally swallowing negotiated protections and distinct claim types. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | DD-012 share register records Harbourglass as holder of 100%; Seller relies on it as evidence of title. | Verify issued capital and ownership against company records and obtain executed transfer instruments, certificates (if applicable), lien releases and corporate approvals/consents at Completion. | **Treat DD-012 as supporting evidence, not conclusive verification** — the register does not itself establish that the shares are free of encumbrances or duly transferable. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller says tax and IP are settled under the general regime. | Negotiate express tax warranties and a tax indemnity with appropriate scope, survival and cap; settle IP ownership, licensing, infringement and chain-of-title warranties and any specific indemnities separately. | **Keep tax and IP open pending express drafting and diligence** — a general cap and unsupported “settled” assertion do not resolve category-specific exposure. |

These are negotiation recommendations, not a substitute for reviewing the full SPA, disclosure materials and diligence record. In particular, the exact claim periods, indemnity scope and Completion mechanics should be checked against the operative clauses and applicable law.
=== END ADVICE ===
